subject.title: Feature request: Session TTL / max lifetime for automatic rotation

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-session max-age/max-turn rotation policy, and if so should it live under session.reset or a new lifecycle/rotation config surface?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes when long-running sessions are destroyed or preserved; automation cannot safely choose the user-visible lifecycle, memory continuity, and compatibility semantics.

options.title: Define Unified Rotation Policy
options.body: Add an explicit maintainer-approved contract for max age, max turns, safe pre-rotation memory handoff, and compatibility tests before implementation.

options.title: Document Existing Controls Only
options.body: Keep daily/idle/manual reset as the supported lifecycle surface and document heartbeat isolation, compaction, and cron hygiene as the supported workaround.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Session Boundary Work
options.body: Defer this issue into the broader session-boundary/context-pressure design so max-age, pruning, and auto-split use one lifecycle model.

recommendation.title: Define Unified Rotation Policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit maintainer-approved contract for max age, max turns, safe pre-rotation memory handoff, and compatibility tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to daily reset, memory flush, and related session lifecycle product history.
